excerpts.abstract:
\begin{abstract}
\noindent
We couple a Cellular Potts Model (CPM) of a multispecies biofilm to OpenMC Monte Carlo photon
transport, and audit what the coupled implementation does and does not support. The one-way path
executes end to end: geometry export, photon transport, constructive-solid-geometry mass
normalisation, dose conversion, coordinate transfer, and cell-, lineage- and generation-level
attribution, with orientation and conservation checks across the exchange boundary. One-way
transfer of a transport code's dose field into a cell-based model is an established, validated
method class, but a targeted search located no prior coupling of OpenMC to a Cellular Potts Model
or to any other cell-scale biological model; every documented OpenMC coupling is to
nuclear-engineering multiphysics. This work therefore extends an established paradigm to a new
transport code and a new biological target rather than introducing the paradigm.

Auditing the CPM's radiation-linked terms against their shipped parameterisation gives two
measured results. The melanin term changes Metropolis acceptance by 13.4\% to 29.2\% across 256 seeds, whereas
the direct per-species radiation term reaches $7.505\times10^{-2}$ in $\Delta H$ (a 1.5\% acceptance bias), about ten
times smaller than the melanin term rather than four orders smaller; only the product of melanin production and melanin
coupling reaches the dynamics, so the two are not separately identifiable. The paper's question is
then put to an ensemble, with the tests declared before it ran: 256 seeds at the published
configuration, each run under four arms of the acceptance rule that zero the direct term, the
melanin production, both, or neither, paired within seed. At the shipped constants, neither term moves a parcel. Switching
the melanin path off shifts the mean radius of the two species it acts on by $+0.0001$ and
$-0.0004$ of the cylinder radius (paired sign tests $p = 0.95$ and $0.75$; the pre-registered
prediction that both move inward was wrong), and switching the direct term off is equivalent to
leaving it on within a pre-registered bound of $0.05$ radii for every species. The direct term itself works: a positive control that amplifies its coefficient $4\times10^{5}$-fold for \textit{C.~neoformans}, at a smaller configuration, moves that species toward the source on average, so for that term the null is consistent with a coefficient too small to act at this configuration within 100~MCS rather than with a missing mechanism. The melanin path has no positive control. The inward drift
every arm shares is adhesion-and-volume relaxation, present with both terms off. The single-seed
radial pattern of earlier versions, a separation of $0.15$ radii between two species, is one draw
from a per-seed spread of standard deviation $0.11$ centred at $-0.006$. The ensemble runs under the
analytic field; the transport path contributes no number to it.

The boundaries are declared rather than discovered late. A proposed partial stochastic
differential equation organises diffusion, directed motility, nutrient, radiation, melanin,
interaction and forcing terms; it is a specification, and the executed simulations---the CPM,
two Langevin programs described once in Methods, and a radial transport solver now in a
companion paper---realise only subsets of it. The CPM represents seven named species as computational biomass parcels rather
than individual organisms, and has neither biomass growth nor a dose-dependent survival process,
so the implemented phenotype is radiotropism and the model cannot test radiotrophy or
radioresistance. The transport workflow is explicitly non-calibrating: no target physical
parameter is inferred and no value is fitted to this system. The parameters are not uniform in
provenance and are not reported as though they were: most are literature priors or values
derived from them, several are flagged as weakly supported, and the melanin coupling through
which radiation actually reaches the acceptance dynamics is a declared modelling choice ---
hard-coded and uncited, and tabulated as such beside every other value the model runs with.

What the work establishes is a reproducible computational foundation, one ensemble answer
about its own acceptance rule, and a specific list of the measurements, uncertainty controls, and
model revisions required before any physical or biological feedback claim can be evaluated.
excerpts.result:
\paragraph{Result.} P1 failed and P2 held. Under full minus $\alpha_M = 0$ the paired mean shift
is $+0.0001\,r/R$ for \textit{C.~neoformans} (129 of 256 seeds positive, $p = 0.95$) and
$-0.0004\,r/R$ for \textit{C.~sphaerospermum} (125 of 256, $p = 0.75$); the prediction that the
melanin path moves both inward was wrong. Under full minus $\beta_{s,\mathrm{ion}} = 0$ the 90\%
interval of the paired mean lies inside the bound for all seven species, the widest being
$[-0.0029, -0.0006]$ for \textit{S.~oneidensis}; the bound is forty times the observed shifts. The direct term's mechanism is not absent: \texttt{tests/deterministic\_radiation.jl} sets $\beta_{s,\mathrm{ion}} = -20$ for \textit{C.~neoformans} and $+20$ for \textit{S.~oneidensis}, $4\times10^{5}$ and about $270$ times their shipped values, and at $N = 24$ with one parcel per species over 60~MCS and five seeds the first moves toward the axis on average and the second away. No such control exists for the melanin path.
Exploratory: full minus both-off is within $\pm0.002\,r/R$ for every species, with within-seed
correlation above $0.98$, so the four arms track one another. All seven species drift from a
seeding frame of about $0.53\,r/R$ to about $0.51\,r/R$ by MCS 100 in every arm, the arm with
both terms off included, so that drift is adhesion-and-volume relaxation. The
\textit{C.~neoformans}--\textit{B.~subtilis} separation is $-0.006\,r/R$ in every arm with a
standard deviation of $0.11$ over seeds; seed 42's $+0.16$ is one draw from that spread
(Figure~\ref{fig:radial}). Figure~\ref{fig:consortium} shows that realisation on the lattice,
under the full model and with both terms off.
excerpts.dose:
The regime in which those inputs are obtainable is not the one this paper's motivating sites
occupy. Section~\ref{sec:planned_feedback} put the gap at about ten orders of magnitude: a
reactor irradiation delivers of order $\mathrm{Gy}\,\mathrm{min}^{-1}$ and the environmental
settings cited in Section~\ref{sec:intro} are closer to $\mathrm{mGy}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, so a sensitivity
constant calibrated in one is not transferable to the other. Engineered nuclear facilities lie
between them, and biofilms are documented there. Sarr\'{o} et al.\ submerged a bioreactor
carrying stainless steel and titanium coupons in a spent nuclear fuel pool at a Spanish nuclear
power plant, characterised the biofilm that developed on both materials, and measured its
radioactivity by gamma-ray spectrometry: the biofilms retained radionuclides from the pool water,
$^{60}$Co in particular \cite{sarro2007}. Karley et al.\ isolated six bacterial species from
spent-fuel-pool water with $D_{10}$ values from 248~Gy to 2~kGy and biofilm-forming capability,
and reported biofilm-mediated Co and Ni removal up to 3.8~$\mu$g per mg of biomass
\cite{karley2018}; a later study of the same isolates --- among them \textit{B.\ subtilis}, one
of the seven modelled here --- found that dead biomass also removed both ions, which is what a
sorption rather than a metabolic mechanism predicts \cite{karley2023}.

\emph{Dose and dose rate are not interchangeable, and the gap here is not marginal.} Writing
damage as a function of accumulated dose alone assumes dose--time reciprocity. In aqueous systems
the dominant damage pathway is indirect, through radiolysis products whose steady-state
concentration is set by competing generation and recombination kinetics --- both rate-dependent.
The regimes involved are far apart: a reactor irradiation delivers of order
$\mathrm{Gy}\,\mathrm{min}^{-1}$, while the environmental settings this work cites as motivation
are closer to $\mathrm{mGy}\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, roughly ten orders of magnitude apart. A
sensitivity constant calibrated in one regime is not transferable to the other by construction,
and that is a statement with a number attached rather than a general caution.

\section*{Author Contributions}
Stated under the CRediT taxonomy. H.K.: conceptualisation, software, investigation, validation,
data curation, writing --- original draft, writing --- review and editing. B.F.: conceptualisation,
methodology, writing --- review and editing. Both authors approved the version submitted. The

\includegraphics[width=0.99\linewidth]{fig_consortium_seed42}
\caption{One realisation of the ensemble configuration, seed 42, $N = 40$, six parcels per
species, under the full model (top) and with both radiation-derived terms off (bottom), at
MCS 0, 50 and 100. The MCS 0 column is the shared seeding frame. Every reported number in this
paper comes from the 256-seed ensemble of Figure~\ref{fig:radial}; this single realisation is
what those curves average over, shown so that the lattice the acceptance rule acts on is in the
paper. Frames were written by \texttt{consortium\_frames.jl} on the machine and commit the
ensemble CSV names, and rendered from them by \texttt{tools/render\_consortium.py}; a video of
the same two arms to MCS 100 is in the repository under \texttt{assets/}.}
